messages:
incident-bot: Pager: SEV2 - CUSTOMER IMPACT - streaming timeouts to customer 'AcmePay' gateway (dedicated pool: rp-dedicated-12) :rotating_light:

sam (oncall): saw it. getting context. is this hitting one tenant or many?

jia (eng-sre): logs show heavy 502/504 from the gateway side. connection resets during websocket handshake + intermittent 0-byte frames. Looks concentrated to rp-dedicated-12 nodes: hostlist: node-22..node-27.

mike (eng-ml): AcmePay has a dedicated pool and private VPC peering. their gateway implements an SSE/WS proxy with a short upstream idle timeout (30s). our streaming keepalives are every 45s for some models.

nina (account): Eli from Acme is on the line, says their customers see stalled streams and repeated reconnects. They have a high-priority payment flow.

eli (cust-eng): (from Acme) Confirming: users see the spinner for ~30s then client reconnects. Our gateway logs: 
```
2026-03-15T14:12:03Z INFO connection_close id=abc123 reason=read_timeout upstream=10.4.5.22:443
2026-03-15T14:12:04Z WARN proxy_retries id=abc123 attempts=3
```
We increased retries and saw more load.

sam (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) page eng-sre + cust-eng in a triage call. 2) shift AcmeTraffic to fallback routing (non-streaming short-poll) for 15m if possible. 3) apply temporary keepalive alignment (client-side) if runtime change is cheap.

jia (eng-sre): triage ack. starting data collection: grabbing tcpdump from node-24 and proxy logs. running script: 
```
/opt/tools/grab_streams.sh --node node-24 --since 10m --out /tmp/acme-dump.tar.gz
```

jia (eng-sre): quick check: per-node connection counts spiked at 14:11:30, and there are repeated TLS renegotiations. Could be our connection reuse to the customer's gateway hitting their proxy limits.

mike (eng-ml): model pipeline also shows occasional long-tail token generation pauses ~>45s at the batching layer when queueing grows. If we can route to a variant that flushes partial responses faster (enable chunked streaming) that might help.

sam (oncall): Can we do a safe runtime tweak to heartbeat interval? We need something low-risk.

mike (eng-ml): yes — runtime flag `--ws-keepalive=20s` exists behind a config toggle. For dedicated pools this is per-pool change: PATCH to pool config. Risk: increases downstream traffic but should be safe for 15m.

jia (eng-sre): I'll prepare the change on node-25 first as a canary. Command: 
```
rbctl pool update rp-dedicated-12 --annotations '{"ws_keepalive":"20s"}' --node node-25
```

ops-bot: deploy-request queued (id: dq-8742). Approve with `/ops approve dq-8742`.

sam (oncall): approved. executing canary.

(90s later)

jia (eng-sre): canary applied on node-25. early telemetry: active connections on node-25 remained stable, and we saw fewer upstream idle closes for those flows.

eli (cust-eng): Acme reports some sessions recovered after ~2m. They still see some reconnect spikes from older sessions.

nina (account): keeping the customer updated: "we've applied a temporary keepalive change and are routing a portion of traffic to fallback while we validate". They asked for ETA.

sam (oncall): ok, plan B if problem persists: 1) Route 100% of Acme traffic through our non-streaming fallback endpoint (no WS) for 15-30m. 2) Increase per-connection limit to reduce proxy churn (if allowed by peering). 3) Open a joint debug session with Acme to inspect their edge proxy config.

mike (eng-ml): routing change prepared: traffic policy `route:acme-fallback` ready. Command to flip: 
```
rbctl routing set acme-org --policy route:acme-fallback --until 2026-03-15T15:00:00Z
```

jia (eng-sre): I'm seeing downstream 502s reduce for node-25 but nodes 22/23 still high. Starting rolling patch to nodes 22..27 with 30s between nodes.

incident-bot: Incident timeline updated. Sev2 -> mitigation in progress.

(5m later)

eli (cust-eng): after more retries and the canary, our metrics show 70% of streams now complete. Still a minority (~5%) hit early timeouts. We can accept short polling for now, but payment UX degrade is noticeable.

nina (account): Acme requests a postmortem and asks if this is tenant isolation related — they want guarantees their other customers not impacted.

sam (oncall): we need to confirm tenant isolation: jia can you confirm whether rerouted traffic affected other tenants on rp-dedicated-12?

jia (eng-sre): checkpoint: routing was targetted by tenant tag; no cross-tenant routing observed. The spike on nodes 22/23 had collateral CPU increase but isolation controls prevented queue stealing. I'll capture metrics and add to incident artifacts.

mike (eng-ml): root cause hypothesis: mismatch between our streaming keepalive and Acme gateway idle timeout causing upstream closes + retry storms; plus occasional batching delays led to >timeout windows. Remediation: align keepalive, offer fallback, and recommend customer increase their upstream timeout or enable connection pooling.

sam (oncall): customer-facing actions: 1) Continue partial routing to fallback for 20m, 2) schedule immediate joint call w/ Acme (ops + cust-eng + Acme infra) to discuss upstream timeouts and connection limits, 3) follow-up PM: assess whether runtime should default to 20s keepalive for dedicated pool customers behind proxies.

ops-bot: route flip executed: `route:acme-fallback` -> 85% traffic now.

(10m later)

eli (cust-eng): after 85% fallback we see successful completion rate 95%. Payment flow reported much better. We'll keep monitoring.

nina (account): confirmed customer satisfied with mitigation but requests SLA credit evaluation for the degraded window.

sam (oncall): logging next steps for postmortem: - collect tcpdumps + proxy logs (node-22..27) - export routing change audit - note timeline and canary results - impact calc (requests affected, error rates) - customer comms drafts.

jia (eng-sre): collecting artifacts to /artifacts/incidents/1893004567/ . will attach perf graphs.

mike (eng-ml): follow-up engineering items: - add config guardrail to warn if keepalive > gateway idle guessed from latency - add per-pool streaming healthcheck - evaluate batching thresholds for long-tail flush.

sam (oncall): handing off to oncall-night: @oncall-night you have the incident. If anything regresses page me.

ops-bot: handoff recorded: sam -> oncall-night at 2026-03-15T15:05:23Z.

(incident-bot): incident transitioned to monitoring. Severity stayed SEV2 during mitigation window.

eli (cust-eng): thx team, we'll stay on standby for the joint call.

nina (account): thanks everyone. I'll prep the customer comms and SLA request template.

sam (oncall): closing this thread from active incident — will convert to postmortem doc and link it here when ready. :white_check_mark:
